stories.title: Meta Ordered to Pay $25 Billion After Court Finds 43 Million Privacy Violations
stories.description: A New Mexico court ordered Meta to pay $25 billion over 43 million privacy-related violations linked to the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

stories.title: Gcore Makes Enterprise Security Bundle Free for Public Agencies Until End of the Year
stories.description: Gcore is offering its WAAP Enterprise plan free of charge to any government body or public agency until December 31, 2026.

stories.title: Major U.S. Banks Detect Unauthorized AI Agents Operating Inside Customer Accounts
stories.description: Major U.S. banks are detecting third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, raising concerns that automated tools could act beyond the instructions customers give them.

stories.title: eMudhra Exits Global SSL/TLS Certificate Business Following the Vulnerability Disclosure
stories.description: eMudhra Limited has announced it is exiting the global SSL/TLS certificate business after disclosing weak private keys in eight intermediate certificate authority certificates.

stories.title: Claude Security Now Scans Repositories Continuously to Find Flaws and Track Fixes
stories.description: Anthropic has updated Claude Security so it can keep checking connected code repositories as they change, rather than waiting for a person to start each scan.

stories.title: Hacker Conversations: Corey Thuen and the Evil Bit
stories.description: Corey Thuen hires hackers for what he calls ‘the evil bit’ — an adversarial streak he believes is either there or it isn’t.

stories.title: INTERPOL Arrests 1,462 Suspects, Disrupts 10,909 Cybercrime Networks in Global Crackdown
stories.description: INTERPOL's Operation Serengeti III disrupted 10,909 malicious networks, arrested 1,462 suspects, and recovered over $105 million.

stories.title: Indurex Raises $8 Million to Expand Industrial Cybersecurity Platform
stories.description: The Amsterdam-based company plans to use the funding for research and development and commercial expansion in Europe and the Middle East.

stories.title: Signal Vulnerability Lets Malicious Callers Block Hang-Ups
stories.description: Affecting the open source calling library RingRTC, the bug prevented calls from ending properly.

stories.title: Tech and Security Companies Respond to PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities
stories.description: Vendors are checking their products for PHP2Shell, security firms are shipping detections, and governments are urging immediate patching.

stories.title: The AI Agent Nobody Owns: Watch Expert Webinar On Your Newest Insider Threat
stories.description: Bitdefender examines shadow AI risks, endpoint visibility gaps, and a malicious agent skill found in the wild.

stories.title: Railway Says Intruder May Have Accessed Customer Secrets, Urges Credential Rotation
stories.description: Railway says an intruder may have accessed decrypted environment variables for some users, as a researcher reports related cryptocurrency theft.
